transcript.text: If your dryer won't stop running, it usually means one of two things: either it is in its final cool-down phase (where it runs without heat to prevent creasing), or there is a fault with the control system keeping it on. First, check if the drum is still turning and if it feels warm. If it has stopped tumbling but the door won't unlock after 10 minutes, that is normal for many modern dryers as they wait for the drum to cool down before releasing the lock. However, if it is still running continuously with heat or noise even when you try to turn it off, please tell me: does it make a faint clicking sound from inside? This helps distinguish between a simple programme end and an electrical fault.
it says End but the drum keeps turning for a bit every few minutes. no clicking that i know of

This intermittent tumbling after the display says 'End' is very likely normal. Many modern dryers run the drum for a few minutes every so often during the final cool-down cycle to prevent creases from setting in while the clothes are still warm. Since there is no clicking sound and it isn't running continuously with heat, your dryer is probably just finishing its programme safely. If you want to stop it immediately, simply turn the dial back to 'Off' or unplug it; otherwise, let it finish and the door should unlock once it has cooled down.
ok but it goes on for about an hour if i leave the clothes in. is that normal? worried its wasting electricity

Yes, that is normal. The hour-long period you are seeing is the final cool-down phase combined with an 'anti-crease' feature. It does not use significant electricity because it is not applying heat during these intervals; it is simply tumbling. If you want to stop it immediately and save power right now, just turn the dial back to 'Off' or unplug the machine.
